Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side. Goal was to align on whether Acme should start on Hosted API or move straight to Dedicated capacity given your latency/throughput targets.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Target p95 latency: ~120ms for ~512-token responses (chat + short completion mix)
- Sustained traffic: ~150 requests/sec (QPS) during business hours
- Peak bursts: ~350–450 req/sec for short windows (1–3 minutes)
- Model: fine-tuned 7B family (int8 quantized in production)
- Priority: minimize tail latency while keeping steady per-token unit costs

Initial recommendation:
- For ramp and early production (validation / pilot), Hosted API is fine — it gives fastest time-to-value and we can route traffic to higher-performance nodes.
- For sustained 150 QPS with p95 ~120ms and those 350–450 burst windows, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the safer option to guarantee consistent latency and avoid noisy-neighbor effects.

What we propose next:
1) Proof-of-concept load test using your model (or a representative replica) to validate p95 at 150 QPS and burst behavior. We'll run two configurations: Hosted (burst on high-tier instance) and Dedicated (reserved pool with autoscale).
2) Engineering sync (Neha + Rishi) to collect test inputs: model artifact, typical sequence length distribution, any caching keys, and test API keys.
3) Draft mutual action plan and timeline — aim for PoC test week of Nov 30 and a decision by mid-December.

Attachments: redwood-latency-throughput-matrix.pdf (matrix of expected p95 by QPS/instance) and acme-maps-load-test-plan.xlsx (proposed test plan).

Can you confirm the traffic numbers above and whether Nov 30 works for a PoC? Also please share procurement contact if we need to scope a short-term Dedicated commit for the PoC.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Samir — quick answers inline and next steps.

> Can you give a ballpark on Dedicated pricing for a short PoC (1–2 weeks)?
We can provide a short-term reserved pool for the PoC. Ballpark depends on instance family and commit level; for a 1–2 week PoC we typically offer an evaluation rate (discounted short-term commit) — I'll have Rishi follow up with the exact number and procurement terms.

> If we go Hosted initially, how many spikes before we'd see degradation?
Hosted is engineered to tolerate typical spikes, but sustained 350–450 QPS bursts (multi-minute) are when you start to see queuing and p95 degradation unless we provision dedicated burst capacity. For the numbers you shared, Hosted can cover short sub-minute bursts fine; for repeated multi-minute bursts we recommend Dedicated.

Next steps:
- Rishi will send a provisional PoC commercial (short-term commit + evaluation rate).
- Neha will schedule the engineering sync to gather model artifact and traffic samples.
- Once we have access, we’ll run the dual-config load test (Hosted vs Dedicated) and deliver a p95 latency report and cost estimate.

Samir / Olivia — can you confirm: (1) approval for Nov 30 PoC week, (2) who on your side will share model artifacts & test data, and (3) procurement contact to receive the short-term quote?

Thanks,
Marissa
